item.description:
The first Shimmer release: a Mac game-streaming client for PCs running Sunshine and for the PS5, built around Picture in Picture and the DualSense. Signed with Developer ID and notarized; installed copies update themselves.

Shimmer is a fork of glimmer 2026.9.0. Everything from ## 2026.9.0 down in this file is upstream glimmer's history.

Picture in Picture

  • ⌃⌥P, or Picture in Picture in the menu bar, moves the stream into macOS's floating PiP window; it can also pop out automatically when you switch apps. Controllers keep playing; the mouse over the PiP window drives the host pointer.
  • Works around the AVKit sample-buffer PiP crop and black-overlay bugs (Apple FB22411168), leaves no ghost Stage Manager tile, and waits for the stream's first frame.
  • The stream can be screen-recorded and screen-shared from the Mac, and Picture in Picture keeps playing while you record. glimmer hid the stream from screen capture, which stopped the PiP picture when a recording began.
  • While you record, the PiP picture no longer stays frozen after a Stage Manager switch or Mission Control. macOS 27.2 stops drawing a video layer during those animations when the screen is being captured, and never resumes on its own; Shimmer now redraws the PiP panel 20 times a second, which restarts it. The half-second pause during the animation itself is the system's - it holds every window on screen - and remains.

PlayStation 5

  • Streams a PS5 over Remote Play through chiaki-ng's libchiaki, into the same window, Picture in Picture, audio and controller path as a PC. A PS5 on the network appears under Nearby; pairing takes a one-time PlayStation Network sign-in and the code from Pair Device. Stream wakes it from rest mode, waits out a console that is still releasing the previous session, and finds it again if its address changes.
  • The DualSense gets the console's light bar, adaptive triggers and haptics; touchpad and motion go back to the console. Over USB the haptics play on the controller's actuators as the console sends them, through a buffer sized from the stream's measured jitter (about 25 ms on a wired Mac). Over Bluetooth they go in the controller's haptics report (DS5Dongle's layout, after SAxense's research), sent the way P5M for Mac does: asynchronously, a few at a time, with the controller at full motor power. macOS's Bluetooth link carries about 33 reports a second on a MacBook, so dense effects can lose some blocks; short ones come through whole. The console's vibration and trigger-effect intensity settings apply.

Controllers

  • Adaptive triggers now work (checked on a USB DualSense against the pad's own trigger-status report). Shimmer's DualSense output report was missing its report ID, so the controller ignored it, and lacked the bits that let trigger effects apply. PC streams send their trigger effects through the same report.

Wi-Fi

  • "Reduce lag spikes on Wi-Fi" is back, without the background helper: the first time, macOS asks for your password once to allow Shimmer to pause AirDrop's Wi-Fi link (awdl0), which it does only while a stream runs over Wi-Fi, restoring it afterwards.

One window

  • Servers, General, Controller and About tabs replace the launcher and the separate Settings window, laid out like a native Mac utility.
  • Servers lists your PCs and PS5s and the ones nearby, pairs them in place, and holds each machine's stream settings. Add by Address takes a PC's or a PS5's IP address or hostname and works out which it is. PCs can show a Linux, Windows, SteamOS or macOS logo.
  • Settings are grouped with clear labels, descriptions and native buttons; the scrolling pages size the window to their content.

Menu bar

  • The icon shows the connected controller and its battery, drawn after Steam's controller glyphs, or the app you're streaming; a pyramid spinner while connecting.
  • The menu is a Liquid Glass panel: the app on the selected server with Stream, Picture in Picture and End Stream, the stream volume, and each server's resolution, frame rate, bitrate and HDR, which unfold in place.

Streaming and input

  • End Stream disconnects and leaves the game running; "Quit the game when the stream ends" ends it on the PC instead.
  • Mouse Off (in the menu) stops forwarding the mouse and never grabs the pointer. The Mac stays awake while a stream runs.
  • A PC's manual address (for example its Tailscale address) is used when the home address isn't reachable. A stream dropped by sleep or a network change no longer leaves a stale error.
  • "Prefer low audio latency" caps the audio playout cushion at 60 ms. Colour on SDR displays is no longer over-saturated.
  • "Game Mode while streaming" raises Bluetooth controller polling, so input arrives about twice as fast.
  • Less CPU at high bitrates: finding the frame boundaries in the incoming video was the largest cost in the app at ~190 Mbps, and now skips most of the bytes it used to read.
  • The app no longer pauses its main thread for ~28 ms every two seconds to ask macOS whether the login item is registered.

Tools

  • shimmerctl: check connectivity, read logs and run test streams, locally or on another Mac over SSH (docs/CLI.md).

Removed

  • glimmer's root Wi-Fi helper daemon (see Wi-Fi above for its replacement). If an earlier build registered it, the first launch marks it unregistered.

Ported from later glimmer releases

  • Identity storage never reads or deletes Keychain items (glimmer 8aaaaa5).
  • AV1 from AMD encoders, which pad 1080p to 1082 rows, decodes instead of failing (glimmer #223 / #224). AV1 sequence headers that carry decoder-model info are read correctly.
  • A DualSense is announced to the PC before any of its input, so Sunshine creates a PlayStation pad with a working touchpad, not an Xbox 360 pad (glimmer #217).
  • Video and audio are accepted only from the paired PC's address.
  • Logs you copy or share, and shimmerctl's view of them, hide PC names, addresses and error details; telemetry names machines by a per-install pseudonym.
  • Audio: a packet that won't decode is concealed instead of dropped, the playout cushion recovers from under-runs without over-growing (gaps no cushion could bridge no longer count), audio FEC survives a misaligned parity packet, and malformed datagrams are dropped before they can reorder playback.
  • Video and pacing: key frames led by AUD/SEI units open the recovery gate, frames lost after a dropped FEC block are reported, a failed FEC rebuild is never sent as a frame with a hole in it, a frame standing above the pacer's target is trimmed, a due frame is released straight from submit, and a vsync is never claimed twice. Fewer allocations per packet.
  • Recovery: keyframe requests back off during a stall and are spaced by the round trip, a stream that receives but never decodes rebuilds once after 30 s, every RTSP wait is bounded, quitting mid-reconnect still ends the game on the PC, a game the PC deliberately ended isn't relaunched, a bitrate downshift can step back up, and control messages are delivered in order.
